fieldMarks: Largest land member of the weasel family, built like a small bear: thick body, short legs, broad head, short ears
Dark brown to black fur with a pale creamy to gold stripe from each shoulder along the flanks to the base of the bushy tail
White or orange patches common on the throat and chest
Adult males about 11–18 kg; females 6–12 kg
behavior: Solitary and wide-ranging; male home ranges can exceed 1,000 km²
Scavenges carrion (often wolf or hunter kills) in winter and hunts small and medium mammals and birds
Marks food and landmarks with urine and musk
Tends to use higher elevations in summer and lower in winter; young are born in snow dens
habitat: Alpine and arctic tundra and boreal and mountain coniferous forest, usually with winter snow cover; in the south limited to large mountain wilderness.
range: Northern Canada and Alaska, retaining its range in the Arctic and western mountain and boreal regions but gone from the prairies and much of southeastern Canada; in the contiguous U.S. essentially limited to the mountains of Idaho, Montana, Wyoming and Washington.
